Definition: middle voice of a primary verb; to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively):--be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie. Compare G5087.
BiblicalUsage: Keimai means to lie, to be laid, to be set: Luke 2:34 has Simeon saying, behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel. John 21:9 says the disciples saw fish laid thereon, and bread. 1 Corinthians 3:11 says other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ. Revelation 21:16 says the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe everything is laid somewhere: the child is set for fall and rising, the foundation is laid once, and the city lies foursquare. I hold that the only foundation that holds is the one already laid, Jesus Christ.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; Paul; John the Apostle; Simeon
